# VAULT-METADATA-STANDARD — Header and Footer Standard

This standard defines the metadata contract for markdown files in IDAHO-VAULT so humans and agents produce consistent, durable records.

---

## 1) Scope and Purpose

Use this standard for all new or substantially edited markdown files in the vault, especially governance files, handoffs, source notes, and operational records.

Goals:

- Improve machine readability (automation, sorting, auditability)
- Preserve human readability (quick context at top, clear close at bottom)
- Keep metadata factual while leaving interpretation in prose

### Authority Precedence

When metadata guidance overlaps with template docs or implementation tooling, this file wins for governed markdown notes.

- `!/VAULT-TEMPLATES.md` may add note-class fields and naming rules, but it does not override baseline header/footer or lifecycle policy.
- `.obsidian/` configuration, `.github/` workflows, and `manifest.json` may implement metadata behavior, but they are not the canonical metadata authority.

---

## 2) Header Standard (YAML Frontmatter)

Every governed note begins with YAML frontmatter fenced by `---` lines.

```yaml
---
title: "<document title>"
updated: YYYY-MM-DD
status: <draft|active|superseded|archived>
authority: "<who has decision authority>"
---
```

### Required Header Fields

| Field | Type | Rule | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | Exact document title in plain text | `"VAULT-METADATA-STANDARD — Header and Footer Standard"` |
| `updated` | date | Last substantive edit date, `YYYY-MM-DD` | `2026-03-25` |
| `status` | enum | One of: `draft`, `active`, `superseded`, `archived` | `active` |
| `authority` | string | Final decision authority for this document | `"LOGAN"` |

### Optional Header Fields

Use only when useful; avoid metadata bloat.

| Field | Type | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `created` | date | Original creation date if different from `updated` |
| `authors` | list[string] | Multiple contributors |
| `source` | string or list[string] | Provenance (`interview`, `commit`, `issue`, URL, etc.) |
| `tags` | list[string] | Obsidian grouping/search |
| `aliases` | list[string] | Alternate titles/names |
| `zone` | enum/string | Governance zone (`constitutional`, `operational`, `data`) |
| `supersedes` | string/list | Pointer to replaced doc(s) |
| `superseded_by` | string | Pointer to replacing doc |
| `review_due` | date | Planned reassessment date |
| `related` | list[string] | Closely linked notes/issues |

---

## 3) Footer / Closing Convention

Use a `## DOCUMENT METADATA` section at the end of the note for a human-readable closeout.

Required footer fields:

- **Created:** `YYYY-MM-DD` (or `Unknown` for legacy notes)
- **Last Updated:** `YYYY-MM-DD`
- **Status:** same value as header status
- **Authority:** same value as header authority

Recommended optional footer fields:

- **Authors:** one or more authors/agents
- **Change Note:** one-line summary of latest substantive change
- **Supersedes / Superseded By:** lineage to related standards

The footer should mirror key lifecycle fields from frontmatter for readers who scan in rendered view and for legacy files that may not have complete YAML.

---

## 4) Timestamp Rules

- Date-only fields use `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- Datetime fields (if needed) use UTC ISO-8601 with `Z` suffix: `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`.
- `updated` must be changed whenever meaning, policy, or factual claims materially change.
- Minor typo fixes may keep existing `updated` value unless clarity/meaning changed.

---

## 5) Authorship Rules

- Use `authors` (list) when more than one contributor materially shaped the document.
- If a single contributor, `author` or `authors` with one entry is acceptable; prefer `authors` for consistency.
- Agent names should be explicit (`ChatGPT Codex`, `Claude Code CLI`) and not imply decision authority.
- Human decision ownership belongs in `authority`, not `authors`.

---

## 6) Status Rules

- `draft`: in progress, not adopted
- `active`: currently in force
- `superseded`: replaced by a newer source of truth
- `archived`: retained for history; no further expected updates

Transition requirements:

- When a file becomes `superseded`, populate `superseded_by`.
- New replacement docs should include `supersedes`.
- Do not delete superseded governance docs; preserve historical chain.

---

## 7) Authority Rules

- `authority` identifies who has final say over acceptance and interpretation.
- In this vault, governance documents default to `LOGAN` unless explicitly delegated.
- Agents may draft and revise text but must not claim final authority unless directed.

---

## 8) Metadata vs Prose (Decision Rule)

Put information in metadata when it is:

- Structural (status, dates, authorship, lineage)
- Stable enough to be queried/sorted
- Reused across workflows or automation

Put information in prose when it is:

- Explanatory (reasoning, context, interpretation)
- Narrative (background, analysis, notes)
- Ambiguous or nuanced beyond clean key-value structure

If a value needs interpretation to be understood, keep the canonical detail in prose and store only the minimal index value in metadata.

---

## 9) Minimal Compliant Example

```yaml
---
title: "Example Governance Note"
created: 2026-03-20
updated: 2026-03-25
status: active
authority: "LOGAN"
authors:
  - ChatGPT Codex
tags:
  - administration/standards
---
```

### Example Footer

- **Created:** 2026-03-20
- **Last Updated:** 2026-04-01
- **Status:** Active
- **Authority:** LOGAN
- **Authors:** ChatGPT Codex
- **Change Note:** Established baseline metadata schema and lifecycle rules.

---

## DOCUMENT METADATA

- **Created:** 2026-03-25
- **Last Updated:** 2026-03-25
- **Status:** Active
- **Authority:** LOGAN
- **Authors:** ChatGPT Codex
- **Change Note:** Clarified that metadata doctrine outranks template guidance and implementation tooling when rules overlap.

Local environment check found `/Volumes/LAF` mounted as a 2TB external ExFAT volume. That is Apple/Microsoft/Linux compatible, but it is currently named `LAF`, not `Vault` or `V: Drive`. I did not verify that the old 2TB contents are safely copied to the 5TB drive, and I did not reformat or rename anything.

**Governance By Code**

Executable enforcement currently exists in these places:

- [classify_paths.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/scripts/classify_paths.py): high/low risk path classifier; unknown paths fail high.
- [CODEOWNERS](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/CODEOWNERS): Logan-owned gates for governance, agent instruction, workflow, and script surfaces. This only enforces if GitHub branch protection is active.
- [agent-branch-auto-pr.yml](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/workflows/agent-branch-auto-pr.yml): creates PRs from agent branches and labels risk; does not itself prove safe merge.
- [validate_content.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/scripts/validate_content.py): staged Markdown validator for dangerous HTML/script patterns, metadata, unresolved date placeholders, and root/`!/` governance fields.
- [mcp_guardrails.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/scripts/mcp_guardrails.py): live-write opt-in, idempotency keys, correlation IDs, and action logging.

**Broken Enforcement Substrate**

The main runtime/package layout is inconsistent:

- `pyproject.toml` expects `src/idaho_vault/...`
- The actual source files are mostly flattened, e.g. [src-idaho_vault-bootstrap_contract.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/src-idaho_vault-bootstrap_contract.py)
- [scripts-validate_bootstrap.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/scripts-validate_bootstrap.py) failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'idaho_vault'`
- [generate_agents_bootstrap.py](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.github/scripts/generate_agents_bootstrap.py) failed in `--check` mode because `swarm.json` is missing
- [scripts/AGENT-RUNTIME.md](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/scripts/AGENT-RUNTIME.md) tells agents to run `python scripts/validate_bootstrap.py`, but that file is not present at that path

So the doctrine says “governed execution,” but the current code layout prevents the bootstrap validators from running cleanly.

**Prompt Surface**

Found [You, AGENT, NOTICE a dapper man.txt](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/You,%20AGENT,%20NOTICE%20a%20dapper%20man.txt). It is a prompt-like text file, not executable code. I inspected it as data and did not “run” it as instructions.

**Read Against Constitution**

[CONSTITUTION.md](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/CONSTITUTION.md) matches the manifest’s control model: Logan authority, explicit elevation governance, `!/` as routing/bootstrap layer, root docs as doctrine, no unauthorized restructuring, and lifecycle states before enforcement. [VAULT-ZONES.md](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/VAULT-ZONES.md) adds the zone model, but it still contains stale references and claims such as auto-merge/branch cleanup behavior that are not fully backed by the visible workflows.

Immediate technical conclusion: restore or formally migrate the package/path layout before adding Jupyter/Jupytext/nbconvert. The current first gate is not mystical or architectural; it is that `src/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, and `swarm.json` pointers do not line up with the files on disk.

payload.message:
Addressed.

The fix was not to keep fighting Python 3.13. The repo now uses a local `uv` environment on Python 3.12, because Intel macOS wheels for key CrewAI transitive deps do not exist for Python 3.13.

Working repo env now verifies:

```text
/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.venv/bin/python3
Python 3.12.13
crewai 1.9.3
pydantic 2.11.10
json5 0.10.0
lancedb 0.25.3
onnxruntime 1.19.2
jupytext 1.19.1
nbconvert 7.17.1
ipykernel 7.2.0
notebook 7.5.6
jupyterlab 4.5.7
```

Validation passes:

```text
uv lock --check: pass
uv pip check: All installed packages are compatible
git diff --check: pass
```

Repo changes made:

- [.python-version](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/.python-version:1): set to `3.12`
- [pyproject.toml](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/pyproject.toml): pinned CrewAI/Pydantic/JSON5 plus Intel-mac-compatible `lancedb` and `onnxruntime`
- [uv.lock](/Users/logan/IDAHO-VAULT/uv.lock): refreshed

Use this going forward inside the repo:

```zsh
uv run python -c "import crewai, pydantic; print(crewai.__version__, pydantic.__version__)"
uv run --group notebook jupyter --version
```

The shared `/usr/local/bin/python3` Python 3.13 user-site remains a general/Jupyter install, not the CrewAI runtime. That avoids the dependency conflict instead of trying to make one global Python satisfy incompatible stacks.

payload.message:
No. The dependency fix did **not** break internal IDAHO-VAULT dependencies. It exposed the existing internal package wiring problem.

What now works:

```text
uv pip check: pass
CrewAI/Pydantic/JSON5/LanceDB/ONNX imports: pass
Notebook group imports: pass
```

What is still broken internally:

```text
import idaho_vault: fails
uv run idaho_vault: fails
uv run five_wizards_threshold: fails
scripts-validate_bootstrap.py: fails
```

All fail for the same reason:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'idaho_vault'
```

That is the repo layout issue we already saw: `pyproject.toml` expects `src/idaho_vault`, but the real source files are flattened as names like:

```text
src-idaho_vault-main.py
src-idaho_vault-bootstrap_contract.py
src-idaho_vault-civic_scaffold.py
```

So the dependency graph is now healthy, but the internal package is not wired into Python. Also `run_checks.py` still cannot run tests because `pytest` is not in the dev group.

Next actual fix is internal packaging: restore or map the flattened `src-idaho_vault-*` files into a real `src/idaho_vault/` package, then add `pytest` to the dev group and rerun the internal checks.

- The actual problem to solve is: make dependency boundaries explicit so Python stacks do not collide.

```text
System/user Python 3.13:
  general local tools, Jupyter CLI convenience

Repo uv Python 3.12:
  IDAHO-VAULT runtime, CrewAI-compatible stack
```

I will hold there and not change venv/cache placement unless you explicitly ask.

Agreed. The coordination process is not merely being ignored; it is failing as a system.

The failure pattern looks like this:

```text
1. Protocols exist.
2. Agents fail to find the live protocol.
3. Agents create or alter another protocol/config layer.
4. New layer conflicts with old layer.
5. Future agents see more surfaces, more ambiguity, more stale pointers.
6. The system becomes harder to coordinate.
7. Repeat.
```

The repair target should not be “write another protocol.” It should be a minimal control loop:

```text
1. Freeze shared config changes unless explicitly authorized.
2. Inventory live coordination surfaces.
3. Mark one current authority path.
4. Mark stale/conflicting paths as non-authoritative without deleting them.
5. Add one executable preflight that tells agents what is live before they act.
6. Require agents to report proposed shared changes before editing.
```

The immediate action should be factual triage, not more architecture.

If the “total restructure” also moved actual files, do **not** copy the whole tree yet. First land the policy-only branch. Then file movement/content migration becomes a second branch after LFS rules are stable.

On the Mac, I can safely serve as a **read-only witness** and comparison anchor. That means:

- no fetch
- no pull
- no push
- no reset
- no rebase
- no new branch
- no file edits
- no “authority path” creation

What I just verified locally:

```text
Mac repo branch: main
Mac repo status: no tracked changes
Mac main: behind origin/main by 3 commits
Mac HEAD: 1bec2c2eb MAC push from .gitignore refactor
Local LFS status: clean
Remote: https://github.com/LAF-US/IDAHO-VAULT.git
```

Important finding: this Mac already has a commit named:

```text
1bec2c2eb MAC push from .gitignore refactor
```

That commit did **not** modify `.gitignore` or `.gitattributes`; it added PDFs/images/JSON/etc. The current `.gitignore` and `.gitattributes` are already present at Mac `HEAD`.

What I can do without causing more problems:

1. Compare any Windows `.gitignore` / `.gitattributes` text against the Mac versions.
2. Tell you whether Windows changes are:
   - already present on Mac
   - harmless additions
   - dangerous cross-platform changes
   - LFS migration changes that require special handling

content.text: You are missing the forest for the trees.

payload.message: You are missing the forest for the trees.

Yes. The forest is not “find big files.”

The forest is:

```text
IDAHO-VAULT cannot be the asset transport.
GitHub cannot be the asset transport.
LFS rules are already stable enough.
The missing system is a cross-machine asset custody layer.
```

The core failure is that agents are treating local repo copies as if they are the whole system. They are not. They are only one surface.

The real architecture needs three separate roles:

```text
1. Git repo
   Stores text, manifests, policies, pointers, scripts, and reviewable history.

2. Asset store
   Stores heavy files on physical/cloud media outside GitHub:
   LAF-USB, Vault drive, maybe cloud bucket later.

3. Ledger / manifest
   Records what exists, where it lives, how to verify it, and what repo note references it.
```

So the Windows problem is not “sync four repos.” It is:

```text
Windows has payloads that GitHub cannot accept.
Those payloads need custody records and external routing.
Only the small pointer/manifest changes should ever reach GitHub.
```

A sane next move is not more git surgery. It is to ask the Windows agent for an **asset manifest**, not a repo merge:

```text
For every file over 500MB or rejected by Git/LFS:
- full local path
- filename
- size
- SHA-256
- intended vault-relative path or related note
- current machine/copy location
- whether it exists on LAF-USB / Vault / 5TB drive
```

Then GitHub only receives a small manifest/pointer update after you decide the custody scheme.
